title: Effectiveness of flat proper-support modules over inverse ring sequences
statement: Let $(A_n)_{n\geq1}$ be an inverse sequence of commutative rings with surjective transition maps whose kernels are locally nilpotent (every element of each kernel is nilpotent), and put $A=\varprojlim_n A_n$. Let $X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a separated finitely presented algebraic space [def-pc-scheme, def-trf-algebraic-space, def-sfb-space-morphism-properties, def-weil-affine-spectrum] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and put $X_n=X\times_A\operatorname{Spec}A_n$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Let $M_n$ be finitely presented quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{X_n}$-modules, flat over $A_n$, with support proper over $A_n$, and specified isomorphisms $M_n\otimes_{A_n}A_{n-1}\simeq M_{n-1}$ for $n\geq2$. Finite presentation means etale locally a cokernel between finite rank free modules. Relative flatness is stalkwise flatness on etale charts over base local rings [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Proper support means $M_n\simeq i_*N$ for a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X_n$ with $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}A_n$ proper and $N$ finite type quasi-coherent [def-sfb-space-proper-quot-functor]. Tensor pullback and quasi-coherent modules use [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors, def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Then there exists a finitely presented quasi-coherent module $M$ on $X$, flat over $A$ with support proper over $A$, and isomorphisms $M\otimes_A A_n\simeq M_n$ compatible with every specified transition isomorphism. No flatness of $X$ over $A$ and no Noetherian hypothesis on the rings is imposed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-inverse-modules-near-special-fibre] to the specified system. It gives an open $W$ containing the common infinitesimal locus $X_0$, a finitely presented quasi-coherent $F$ on $W$, and compatible isomorphisms $F\otimes_A A_n\simeq M_n$. In particular every $X_n$ factors through $W$.

source.place: Tag 0CXB, first paragraph; local realization supplied by Tags 0CX5--0CX9.

proof.text: The first reduction of $F$ is $M_1$, whose support is proper. Apply [lem-sfb-space-inverse-module-proper-shrinking] to this local model and replace $W$ by the resulting $W'$. The restrictions of all the isomorphisms in Step 1 still have the same domains $X_n$, since $|X_n|=X_0\subseteq W'$. Now $F$ has proper support over $A$.

source.place: Tag 0CXA, as used in the first paragraph of 0CXB.

proof.text: Choose a proper closed carrier $i:Z\hookrightarrow W$ and $G$ with $F\simeq i_*G$, using the proper-support convention of [def-sfb-space-proper-quot-functor]. The composite $k:Z\to X$ is a closed immersion: its graph in $Z\times_A X$ is closed by separatedness of $X/A$, and the projection $Z\times_A X\to X$ is closed after every base change by properness of $Z/A$ [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Thus $k$ has closed image $C$. It is already a closed immersion over the open $W$ and has empty preimage over $X\setminus C$, so the two opens $W$ and $X\setminus C$ prove the closed-immersion assertion locally. Define $M=j_*F$ for $j:W\hookrightarrow X$ [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. On $W$ it is $F$; on $X\setminus C$ it is zero, since $F$ is carried by $Z$. These restrictions show that $M$ is quasi-coherent and finitely presented: use a finite presentation of $F$ on each etale chart over $W$ and the zero presentation off $C$ [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Also $M=k_*G$, so it has a proper closed carrier on $X$. Since each $X_n$ lies in $W$, the original compatible isomorphisms give $M\otimes_A A_n\simeq M_n$.

source.place: Tag 0CXB, last paragraph (performed before flattening); open-cover verification of extension.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-proper-support-universal-flattening] to $X/A$ and $M$. Its hypotheses hold: $X/A$ is separated and finitely presented, and Step 3 made $M$ finitely presented with proper support. Obtain a scheme monomorphism $h:T\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ of finite presentation which represents flatness of tensor pullback. For every $n$, the reduction $M\otimes_A A_n\simeq M_n$ is flat over $A_n$ by hypothesis. The stated universal property therefore gives a unique factorization $\operatorname{Spec}A_n\to T$.

The monomorphism $h$ is locally of finite type because it is of finite presentation: on affine charts its finitely many algebra generators and relations in particular give finitely many generators. Apply [lem-sfb-nilpotent-tower-monomorphism-rigidity] to the factorizations for every $n$. It makes $h$ an isomorphism. The identity of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ now factors through $h$, so the universal property of [lem-sfb-space-proper-support-universal-flattening] says that $M$ itself is flat over $A$. Together with Step 3 this gives the required module and all the specified transition compatibilities.
